subject: arts-music
unit_title: Elements and Principles of Art and Music
essential_question: How can understanding elements and principles of art and music help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery of melody and pitch through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of melody and pitch.
Check, revise, or improve work about melody and pitch using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about melody and pitch.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Mastery work on melody and pitch. Mastery: organize events, marks, sounds, words, objects, or movements through melody and pitch, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Complete the bounded study yourself before asking for a cue.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses sound (melody and pitch). You do not have to hear it to do it. You may use a written or drawn version, feel the beat by tapping or watching, or read the notes on paper instead.
This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting melody and pitch.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce melody and pitch to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one sequence relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact sequence evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply melody and pitch under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on melody and pitch rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one sequence relationship while working on melody and pitch.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.
